turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Madam Tan. I'm Dr. Lim from the anesthesia team. I'll be looking after you during your surgery today. Let me go through some questions to make sure everything's in order, okay?

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Can you tell me briefly why you're having this surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I've been having bad stomach pains on the right side, especially after eating. The scans showed gallstones, so they want to remove the gallbladder laparoscopically.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Are you currently taking any medications?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes. I take combined oral contraceptive pills—ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone—every day. And I was on amoxicillin 500mg twice daily for a chest infection, but I stopped that two days ago as instructed.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Do you have any allergies to medications, especially antibiotics like penicillin?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh, yes! I had a bad rash all over my body once when I took penicillin for a tooth infection. It was terrible, so I avoid all penicillin now.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Important to know. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, doctor. I had my last sip of water at 7 a.m., like the nurse instructed.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Have you had any anesthesia before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, once for a hernia repair. I woke up fine, just a bit sleepy. No problems at all.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Lastly, are you able to carry out your daily activities without difficulty?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Mostly, lah. The gallbladder pains come and go, but I can still walk, climb stairs, and do housework unless it's a bad day.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you, Madam Tan. We'll proceed with general anesthesia using a Laryngeal Mask Airway as planned. You'll get propofol and fentanyl for induction, sevoflurane for maintenance, and local anesthesia at the port sites. Any questions for me?
